Implementation Plan

Plan: process `analysis/workflow-optimization-2026-10-01.md` into the recommendation-processing report, then delete it (Refs #8796)

Planning ref: `orchestrator/project-8796` at `740ab9242bf7763acf0ce71341c8ecd3c167a6c8` (Integration branch mismatch: false). Source commit to record: `1bf09113182d30722de27cf62619001aa7e7c678`.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends recommendation-processing-report.md per-doc ledger entry format
Scope-mode justification: The issue spells out exactly two file operations: delete one source doc and append one ledger entry. Its verdicts are pre-decided, and I checked each one against the current tree (see "Verification already done"). The report already has a fixed per-doc format: the `### \`analysis/workflow-optimization-2026-09-30-2.md\`` entry at line 1811, a heading, `Source doc:`, `Processed:`, `Source commit:` and a three-column table. This plan reuses that format without change. Neither file can be done more fully than the issue already asks, so there is no wider option to weigh. Widening the change, for example to fix the `Processed source docs (128)` header (see Risks), would break the issue's "Edit only the two files" and "leave that list alone" rules. The order of §6 (Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed) favours an accurate, grep-checked ledger over any extra cleanup.

## Files likely to change
- `analysis/workflow-optimization-2026-10-01.md` (deleted)
- `analysis/recommendation-processing-report.md` (append-only, at end of file)

## Functions or modules to implement
None. This is a docs and ledger change only. No script, workflow, test or scheduler wiring changes (§20: it only modifies existing files, adds no new script or supervisor, and needs no registry entry).

Steps for the implementer:
1. Delete `analysis/workflow-optimization-2026-10-01.md`.
2. Append one new section to the very end of `analysis/recommendation-processing-report.md`. The file currently ends with `...The doc says "No findings." |\n`. Add one blank line, then the block below. Do not change any byte above it.
3. Leave the `## Processed source docs (128)` list (lines 5–136) alone. It does not list `analysis/workflow-optimization-2026-09-30-2.md`; its last bullet is `analysis/workflow-optimization-2026-09-26.md`. Under rule 3 of the issue, that means the list stays unchanged.
4. Do not read, touch or delete any other path under `analysis/`. That includes `last_collection_timestamp.txt`, `validation-selftest-status.json` and the other `workflow-optimization-*.md` docs.

The entry to append (use the current UTC date for `Processed:`; expected `2026-11-04`). Escape any literal `|` inside a cell as `\|`:

The implementer may adjust wording to match the doc's own phrasing after reading it. It must keep every verdict and every checked fact.

## Data structures affected
- Report markdown only: one new `###` section with a three-column table at end of file.
- No JSON, DB, env-var, log-prefix or identifier changes.

## API or interface changes
None. `scripts/apply_analysis_on_main.sh` (line 341) runs `grep -qF -- "<basename>"` on the report to skip docs already processed. The new heading adds `workflow-optimization-2026-10-01.md`, so the dispatcher treats this doc as processed. That is the intended effect.

## Decisions
### D1 — Leave `## Processed source docs (128)` unchanged
- Chosen: do not add the doc to the list or bump N.
- Alternatives considered: add `analysis/workflow-optimization-2026-10-01.md` to the list and bump the count; also fix the header count.
- Why: rule 3 of the issue makes the list update depend on `analysis/workflow-optimization-2026-09-30-2.md` already being listed. It is not listed (last bullet is `-09-26.md`), so the list stays as it is.
